title: The Rescue of the Tin Woodman, part 4
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “Why didn’t you walk around the hole?” asked the Tin Woodman.
“I don’t know enough,” replied the Scarecrow cheerfully. “My head is stuffed with straw, you know, and that is why I am going to Oz to ask him for some brains.”
“Oh, I see,” said the Tin Woodman. “But, after all, brains are not the best things in the world.”
“No, my head is quite empty,” answered the Woodman. “But once I had brains, and a heart also; so, having tried them both, I should much rather have a heart.”
“And why is that?” asked the Scarecrow.
“I will tell you my story, and then you will know.”
So, while they were walking through the forest, the Tin Woodman told the following story:

“I was born the son of a woodman who chopped down trees in the forest and sold the wood for a living. When I grew up, I too became a wood-chopper, and after my father died I took care of my old mother as long as she lived. Then I made up my mind that instead of living alone I would marry, so that I might not become lonely.

“There was one of the Munchkin girls who was so beautiful that I soon grew to love her with all my heart. She, on her part, promised to marry me as soon as I could earn enough money to build a better house for her; so I set to work harder than ever. But the girl lived with an old woman who did not want her to marry anyone, for she was so lazy she wished the girl to remain with her and do the cooking and the housework. So the old woman went to the Wicked Witch of the East, and promised her two sheep and a cow if she would prevent the marriage. Thereupon the Wicked Witch enchanted my axe, and when I was chopping away at my best one day, for I was anxious to get the new house and my wife as soon as possible, the axe slipped all at once and cut off my left leg.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Tin Woodman's father?

A tinsmith in a Munchkin village
A farmer who kept sheep and a cow
A servant of the Wicked Witch

questions.prompt: Per the passage, whom did the Tin Woodman care for after his father died?
options: His old mother
His younger brother
The Munchkin girl
The old woman

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Munchkin girl promise?
options: To marry him once he could build a better house
To wait for him until the old woman died
To leave the old woman's house that same year
To ask the Wicked Witch to bless the marriage

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the old woman promise the Wicked Witch?
options: Two sheep and a cow
A house and a field
Her own silver shoes
A year of service

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the enchanted axe cut off first?
options: His left leg
His right leg
His left arm
His head

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the old woman want to stop the marriage?
options: She was lazy and wanted the girl's cooking and housework
She had promised the girl to a Munchkin farmer
She disliked woodmen and their trade
She feared the girl would be poor if she married

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Tin Woodman say he would rather have a heart than brains?
options: He has had both, and knows which he misses
He has been told brains are useless in Oz
The Scarecrow has already claimed the brains
A heart is the easier of the two to give

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why was the woodman working harder than ever?

The Wicked Witch had set him a task
His mother had left him her debts

Made of tin instead of iron and steel
Blessed so that his work would go faster

A woodman explains why he gave up his trade
A quarrel between two Munchkin families ends badly
A witch punishes a woodman for cutting her trees

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Tin Woodman say is in his head now?
options: Nothing; it is quite empty
Straw, like the Scarecrow's
Tin, poured in by the tinsmith

Angrily, accusing Dorothy of not watching

options: Stop it from ever taking place
Delay it for a year or two
Refuse to attend the wedding
Make the couple regret it

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A tin man begins the story of how he lost his heart
